descriptors.definition: Valuation of company assets and net worth must be executed by certified professional valuers appointed by the audit committee or Board. These practitioners must uphold impartiality, exercise due diligence, and avoid conflicts of interest regarding the target assets.
inclusion: Property, stocks, shares, debentures, securities, and goodwill valuation
Appointment procedures via audit committee or Board
exclusion: Valuation undertaken by individuals with a direct or indirect interest within three years prior or post-appointment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general financial auditing by its specific focus on asset and liability valuation under statutory valuation standards.

descriptors.definition: Valuers who breach compliance rules face monetary fines, while fraudulent contraventions trigger imprisonment terms and mandatory restitution. Convicted valuers are legally compelled to refund their professional remuneration and cover third-party damages arising from misleading statements.
inclusion: Punishment and imprisonment terms for fraud
Liability for remuneration refund and damage payouts
exclusion: Non-fraudulent administrative errors not amounting to statutory rule contraventions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general corporate penalties under Section 450 by providing specialized clawback and damage mechanisms specific to valuation misconduct.

descriptors.concept_name: Registrar Power to Remove Company Names
descriptors.definition: The Registrar may initiate company strike-off procedures when an entity fails to commence business within one year, remains inactive for two consecutive financial years without dormant status, or omits mandatory incorporation filings. Alternatively, a company can voluntarily apply for name removal after extinguishing all liabilities through special resolution or high-threshold member consent.
inclusion: Involuntary strike-off due to non-commencement or operational inactivity
Regulatory body approvals for specialized corporate entities
exclusion: Companies holding valid active operations or holding active dormant status applications
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from formal winding up or liquidation because strike-off is an administrative registry clearance rather than an insolvency resolution process.

descriptors.definition: Government companies wherein the Central Government is a member must prepare annual reports on their working and affairs within three months of their annual general meeting. These reports, along with Comptroller and Auditor-General audit comments, must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
inclusion: Preparation of annual working and affairs reports
Tabling reports and audit comments before Parliament
exclusion: Non-governmental private corporate entities lacking government shareholding thresholds
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from standard private company filing requirements due to the mandatory requirement of parliamentary presentation and auditor-general oversight.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government holds statutory authority to declare specific entities as Nidhi or Mutual Benefit Society and modify how corporate enactments apply to them. Proposed modifications must be laid in draft before Parliament for review prior to final notification issuance.
inclusion: Parliamentary review of draft modification notifications
Application scope covering historical and newly incorporated Nidhi entities
exclusion: Standard commercial companies operating outside mutual benefit frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Differs from normal public or private companies because Nidhi operations are subject to tailored regulatory modifications and parliamentary oversight specific to mutual savings.

descriptors.concept_name: Punishment for Fraud and Residual Penalties
descriptors.definition: Fraud involving specified financial thresholds or public interest carries strict mandatory minimum imprisonment terms and proportional monetary fines scaling with the amount involved. For general corporate violations where no explicit penalty is provided elsewhere in the legislation, residual penal provisions apply.
inclusion: Punishment framework for fraud with monetary or public interest triggers
Legal definitions of wrongful gain and wrongful loss
General penalties for statutory defaults lacking specific assigned punishments
exclusion: Infractions governed by independent, specific penalty sections within the Act
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes high-severity dishonest acts carrying mandatory jail terms from lower-severity technical defaults penalized under residual catch-all provisions.
